name: Bamboo Plot Tokenization
description: Real-world-asset tokenization of sustainable bamboo cultivation plots (ERC-20) where the total token supply for a plot represents 100% fractional ownership of that plot's yield rights — investors buy tokens for any fraction of a registered plot. Minting registers a new plot's shares against a verified land/cultivation record (gated behind maker-checker approval, since it asserts both land rights and a carbon claim). Transfers double as the on-chain chain-of-custody record as physical custody of the harvested bamboo passes from grower to processor to distributor to retailer — the current token holder is the current custodian, timestamped and anchored by the platform's existing audit trail. Burning retires a plot's shares (e.g. on full buyout or end-of-life). Freeze places a compliance hold on an account.

plotId.description: Registry identifier for the specific bamboo plot/parcel — enforced unique so one plot is tokenized only once

species.description: Bamboo species cultivated, e.g. Bambusa balcooa, Dendrocalamus strictus

cooperativeOrGrower.description: Cultivating entity — cooperative, farmer collective, or individual grower

totalShares.description: Total token supply that represents 100% fractional ownership of this plot — a holder's fraction of the plot is their balance divided by this figure

cultivationStartDate.description: Date cultivation began on this plot (YYYY-MM-DD)

certificationBody.description: Sustainable-cultivation certification authority, e.g. FSC, organic certifier

certificateUrl.description: Off-ledger link to the cultivation/sustainability certificate (only its hash lives on-ledger)

certificateHash.description: SHA-256 of the certificate (pins the off-ledger document as proof of origin)

co2SequesteredTonsPerYear.description: Verified or estimated CO2e sequestered by this plot in the CURRENT monitoring period only (tonnes) — a bamboo clump's annual sequestration is not constant: it ramps for years 1-8 then plateaus near equilibrium (aboveground biomass stops growing once harvest offsets recruitment), so this figure changes attestation to attestation. Never multiply this by 30 to project lifetime volume — that overstates true yield by roughly 3.5x. See the linked carbon-credit asset's netTco2ePerHaLifetime for the declining-curve lifetime figure.

carbonMethodology.description: Carbon-accounting methodology applied, e.g. a Verra AR/ALM methodology reference

carbonVerifier.description: Third party that verified the carbon sequestration claim

linkedCarbonCreditAssetId.description: Asset id of the carbon-credit (VCU) instrument separately minted against this plot's verified sequestration, if any — the plot token and its carbon credits are independently tradable, this field only records the link

landClass.description: PRIVATE or REVENUE_NON_FOREST land only — forest land is permanently ineligible for carbon crediting (transit-permit exemption and clean tenure both depend on non-forest status). Optional; only relevant to plots pursuing a carbon claim.

baselineLanduse.description: Land use in the ≥10-year period before this plot was planted — DEGRADED, FALLOW, CROPLAND or BUND. This is the core additionality evidence a validator asks for first: why wasn't bamboo already the rational crop choice here without carbon revenue. Optional; only relevant to plots pursuing a carbon claim, and must be captured at enrolment — a plot enrolled without it cannot retrofit this evidence later.

plantingGeometry.description: BUND (field-boundary planting), INTERCROP (scattered among another crop), or BLOCK (contiguous plantation over 1 hectare). Determines which carbon quantification approach applies: BUND/INTERCROP plots use CENSUS_BASED (this plot registry already IS the census — every clump enumerated and geo-located), while BLOCK plantations require AREA_BASED accounting with matched control plots. Optional; only relevant to plots pursuing a carbon claim.

carbonRegistryBinding.description: Which carbon registry this plot's sequestration is (or will be) credited under — NONE, VERRA_VM0047, BEE_CCTS, or GOLD_STANDARD. A plot should bind to exactly one registry for its whole crediting period; the same tonne credited twice under two registries is double-counting. This field only RECORDS that choice — the platform does not enforce one-way binding or reject a second registry's claim against the same plot; treat it as a declared commitment to check manually, not a guarantee.
